newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat edges back in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat edges back in quiet session.

text.p: Australian wheat futures edged back further in unexpectedly quiet trading on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Friday.
January 1997 was the only futures contract to trade, falling by A$1.50 to A$175.00 in one traded lot.
Options captured slightly more attention, with four call options trading in A$190 January at a A$5 premium and eight call options trading in A$210 January at a A$1.50 premium.
Sam Mende of McIntosh Futures Ltd said there was enough movement overnight in U.S. markets to spark some volume, but this failed to occur.
The looming weekend left futures trading very quiet across all markets, he said.
The A$210 calls at A$1.50 were cheapish, indicating the trader was simply receiving premium. The A$190 trade at A$5.00 was just a volatility trade, he said.
The quiet SFE session followed wheat futures declines in Chicago overnight on USDA confirmation that world wheat stocks were rising.
World ending stocks for 1996/97 would total 117.43 million tonnes, up from 108.68 million tonnes forecast in August, the USDA said.
